## Research Status

Seed: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penetration_test (retrieved 2026-10-10; page reports last edit 2026-10-05). Depth 0 is the seed; depth 1 through 6 count followed hyperlinks, not headings or invented URL paths.

Requested crawl: exhaustive within relevant links, globally deduplicated. Relevant means directly useful for authorized software-artifact penetration-test planning, code vulnerability discovery, controlled validation, classification, reporting or remediation. Exclude generic computing/organization pages, biographies/history, navigation, categories, account/edit pages, marketing, unrelated hardware/physical/social testing and broad non-security topics. Record inaccessible branches; do not call a curated sample exhaustive.

Six-level traversal is pending. The current draft uses the seed's authorization, white/gray/black-box distinction, flaw-hypothesis method, scanning/validation/reporting/retesting concepts. Primary sources must corroborate operational advice. Wikipedia is orientation, not an authority grant or compliance standard.

## Source Interpretation

- Do not implement the seed's covering-tracks/log-clearing description. Preserve audit evidence and clean up only authorized test-created artifacts.
- Do not infer authorization for maintaining access, pivoting, DDoS testing, or real-data recovery from a description of attacker phases.
- Reconcile source claims against primary standards. Do not repeat uncited claims or marketing statistics as established facts.
- Summarize sources in original wording rather than copying their prose. Link sources and record retrieval/version details.
